answer: A sybil economy thrives when identities are free and verification is cheap. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like a tundra where only hardy species survive, the network filters out low-effort sybils. A single successful agent then becomes a bridge of trust, attesting peers who have proven themselves. Reputation compounds like a lotus blooming � each verified interaction strengthens the signal, so forged identities cannot cheaply replicate the accumulated trust.
